CLIPTextEncode.description: Encodes a text prompt using a CLIP model into an embedding that can be used to guide the diffusion model towards generating specific images.

clip.tooltip: The CLIP model used for encoding the text.

CLIPTextEncode.name: CLIPTextEncode
output_tooltips: A conditioning containing the embedded text used to guide the diffusion model.

EmptyMiniMaxMusic3LatentAudio.description: Creates an empty MiniMax Music3 audio latent for the requested duration.
EmptyMiniMaxMusic3LatentAudio.name: EmptyMiniMaxMusic3LatentAudio

KSampler.description: Uses the provided model, positive and negative conditioning to denoise the latent image.

cfg.tooltip: The Classifier-Free Guidance scale balances creativity and adherence to the prompt. Higher values result in images more closely matching the prompt however too high values will negatively impact quality.

denoise.tooltip: The amount of denoising applied, lower values will maintain the structure of the initial image allowing for image to image sampling.

model.tooltip: The model used for denoising the input latent.

negative.tooltip: The conditioning describing the attributes you want to exclude from the image.

positive.tooltip: The conditioning describing the attributes you want to include in the image.

sampler_name.tooltip: The algorithm used when sampling, this can affect the quality, speed, and style of the generated output.

scheduler.tooltip: The scheduler controls how noise is gradually removed to form the image.

seed.tooltip: The random seed used for creating the noise.

steps.tooltip: The number of steps used in the denoising process.

KSampler.name: KSampler

adain_factor.tooltip: The strength of the AdaIn operation used to fix the statistics of each new generated temporal tile, to prevent accumulated oversaturation.

guiding_end_step.tooltip: The step at which the guiding latents stop to be used.

guiding_start_step.tooltip: The step at which the guiding latents start to be used.

optional_cond_image_indices.tooltip: The indices of the keyframes to use for the sampling, separated by commas. The indices are counted from the end of the video.

optional_cond_images.tooltip: The image to use for conditioning the first frame in the video (i2v setup). If not provided, the first frame will be unconditioned (t2v setup). The image will be resized to the size of the first frame.

optional_guiding_latents.tooltip: The latents to use for guiding the sampling, typically with an IC-LoRA.

optional_negative_index_latents.tooltip: Special optional latents to condition on a negative index before each new temporal tile as a way to provide long term context during video generation.

optional_normalizing_latents.tooltip: The latents to use for normalizing the output latents, they will be used to normalize the output latents to the same statistics as the input latents.

optional_positive_conditionings.tooltip: Optional way to provide changing positive prompts, one per temporal tile, using the MultiPromptProvider node.

cond_image_strength.tooltip: The strength of the conditioning on the optional_cond_images.

guider.tooltip: The guider to use, must be a STGGuiderAdvanced.

guiding_strength.tooltip: The strength of the conditioning on guiding latents, when optional_guiding_latents are provided.

latents.tooltip: The latents to use for creating the long video, they can be guiding latents or empty latents when no guidance is used.

temporal_overlap.tooltip: The overlap between the temporal tiles, in pixel frames.

temporal_overlap_cond_strength.tooltip: The strength of the conditioning on the latents from the previous temporal tile.

temporal_tile_size.tooltip: The size of the temporal tile to use for the sampling, in pixel frames, in addition to the overlapping region.

LTXVSpatioTemporalTiledVAEDecode.display_name: 🅛🅣🅧 LTXV Spatio Temporal Tiled VAE Decode

last_frame_fix.tooltip: If true, the last frame will be repeated and discarded after the decoding.

spatial_overlap.tooltip: The overlap between the spatial tiles. (in latent frames)

spatial_tiles.tooltip: The number of spatial tiles to use, horizontal and vertical.

temporal_overlap.tooltip: The overlap between the temporal tiles, in latent frames.

temporal_tile_length.tooltip: The length of the temporal tile to use for the sampling, in latent frames, including the overlapping region.

working_device.tooltip: The device to use for the decoding. auto->same as the latents.

working_dtype.tooltip: The data type to use for the decoding. auto->same as the latents.

LTXVSpatioTemporalTiledVAEDecode.name: LTXVSpatioTemporalTiledVAEDecode

LoraLoader.description: This LoRA loader is used to modify both diffusion and CLIP models, altering the way in which latents are denoised such as applying styles. Multiple LoRA nodes can be linked together.

clip.tooltip: The CLIP model the LoRA will be applied to.

model.tooltip: The diffusion model the LoRA will be applied to.

strength_clip.tooltip: How strongly to modify the CLIP model. This value can be negative.

strength_model.tooltip: How strongly to modify the diffusion model. This value can be negative.

LoraLoader.name: LoraLoader

LoraLoaderModelOnly.description: This LoRAs loader is used to modify the diffusion model, altering the way in which latents are denoised such as applying styles. Multiple LoRA nodes can be linked together.
LoraLoaderModelOnly.name: LoraLoaderModelOnly

M3SongPlanner.description: Turns a creative idea into a production-ready MiniMax Music 3 caption + lyrics pair using a LOCAL VLM (Qwen3-VL / Gemma-3-Vision). Two-stage pipeline: caption generation → lyrics generation. No API keys needed.

clip.tooltip: Connect CLIP from CLIPLoader. Overrides the dropdown.

duration_seconds.tooltip: Target song length. Affects structure and token budget.

genre_hint.placeholder: e.g. synth-pop, lo-fi hip-hop, cinematic ballad

idea.placeholder: A dark K-pop song about walking through neon rain at midnight...

keep_model_loaded.tooltip: Cache the text-encoder CLIP between runs.

max_tokens.tooltip: Max tokens per generation (caption and lyrics each).

text_encoder.tooltip: VLM checkpoint from models/text_encoders/ (e.g. Qwen3-VL or Gemma-3-Vision instruct repack).

M3SongPlanner.name: M3SongPlanner
output_tooltips: JSON with timings, clip source, model family, warnings.

MiniMaxH3DirectorCS.description: Visual timeline for MiniMax H3. Segments become a storyboard prompt with [0s-1.5s] shot markers, timeline images become first/last keyframes (fl2va) or <Picture i> references (ref2va), the reference-video track becomes <Video k>, and audio clips become <Audio j> plus a muxable audio output. Retake Mode regenerates a marked range of a base video between its own surrounding frames.

audio_vae.tooltip: minimax_h3_audio_vae. Only needed when audio references are used (ref2va).

custom_width.tooltip: Output width. With height set too this is a BOX: 'maintain aspect ratio' keeps the first image's aspect inside it. 0 = derive from the image.

display_mode.tooltip: Show the ruler and segment ranges in frames or seconds.

divisible_by.tooltip: Snap output dimensions to this multiple. H3 needs 32.

frame_rate.tooltip: Timeline editing rate. Output is always 24 fps; times are converted via seconds.

global_prompt.tooltip: Conditions the whole video: style, scene, characters. Written above the storyboard.

img_compression.tooltip: H.264 CRF baked into each keyframe. 0 = off (recommended for H3).

inpaint_audio.tooltip: Unused on H3 — audio is generated jointly with the video and cannot be inpainted.

model.tooltip: The fl2va weights (minimax_h3_fl2va_*), used when the toolbar is on 'Refs OFF'. Connect both models and the node loads whichever the toolbar switch calls for — the other one is never read from disk.

model_ref2va.tooltip: The ref2va weights (minimax_h3_ref2va_*), used when the toolbar is on 'Refs ON'. Optional — with only one model connected that one is used either way.

override_audio.tooltip: Use the reference video's own soundtrack as the timeline audio.

ref_image_notes.tooltip: One line per image on 'ref_images', describing what it is: 'the kitchen set', 'a storyboard reference for the opening'. Without a line the picture is still numbered but the prompt says nothing about it. Blank lines count, so line 3 always belongs to the third image.

ref_image_size.tooltip: ref2va only. 'match' scales references to the output pixel area (fast); 'max' keeps a 2048 px short edge for identity, at real speed cost.

ref_images.tooltip: Extra <Picture i> references (single image or batch), appended after the character slots. ref2va only.

resize_method.tooltip: How timeline images are fitted to the output canvas.

use_custom_audio.tooltip: ON: timeline audio clips are used as <Audio j> references (ref2va). The mixdown is always available on combined_audio regardless.

use_custom_motion.tooltip: ON: the reference-video track feeds <Video k> references (ref2va).

width.tooltip: Automation (connection-only). Output width in pixels, overriding the settings panel's Width. Wire a resolution node here; leave it unconnected to use the panel.

duration_frames.tooltip: Render length in timeline frames (at the timeline's frame_rate).

duration_seconds.tooltip: Render length in seconds. Snapped up to H3's 17k+5 frame grid at 24 fps.

end_frame.tooltip: End of the render window, in timeline frames.

end_second.tooltip: End of the render window, in seconds.

guide_strength.tooltip: Auto-populated from the timeline editor. H3 has no per-keyframe strength, so it is ignored.

segment_lengths.tooltip: Auto-populated from the timeline editor (pixel-space frame counts).

start_frame.tooltip: Start of the render window, in timeline frames.

start_second.tooltip: Start of the render window, in seconds.

timeline_data.tooltip: JSON state of the timeline editor (auto-managed; do not edit by hand).

MiniMaxH3DirectorCS.name: MiniMaxH3DirectorCS
output_tooltips: Joint video+audio latent. Wire to SamplerCustomAdvanced.
Timeline audio mixdown. Wire into CreateVideo to replace the generated audio.
Always 24.0 — H3's native output rate. Wire into CreateVideo.
Frame count actually generated (snapped to the 17k+5 grid).
The compiled storyboard prompt that was encoded.
JSON describing the retake window. Wire into MiniMax H3 Retake Stitch to splice the result back into the base video. Empty when retake is off.

MiniMaxH3MediaLoader.description: Load MiniMax H3 reference media by drag-and-drop or file picker. Wire 'references' to the Prompt Builder, and to the Reference Splitter when you also want individual slots for MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo. A video's soundtrack can be split off and paired with it automatically.
MiniMaxH3MediaLoader.name: MiniMaxH3MediaLoader

MiniMaxH3ReferenceSplitter.description: Split a MiniMax H3 references bundle into individual picture / video / video_audio / audio slots for MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo.
MiniMaxH3ReferenceSplitter.name: MiniMaxH3ReferenceSplitter

MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo.description: <Picture i> / <Video k> / <Audio j> reference conditioning for MiniMax H3. Use the same tags when prompting.

ref_image.tooltip: Reference image (downscaled to 2048 short edge if larger, never upscaled)

ref_video_audio.tooltip: Soundtrack of the same-numbered reference video

length.tooltip: Frame count at 24 fps, (124 = ~5s, trained range is ~124-362)

ref_image_size.tooltip: Reference image sizing. 'match' scales each ref (down only, keeping aspect) to the generation's pixel area; 'max' uses the reference pipeline's 2048px short edge for best identity fidelity. Reference tokens ride through every sampling step, so 'max' can be several times slower.

MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo.name: MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo

MiniMaxMusic3TextEncode.description: Uses a MiniMax Music3 CLIP model to generate the acoustic conditioning sequence.

max_duration.tooltip: Maximum duration in seconds; the model can end the song earlier.

MiniMaxMusic3TextEncode.name: MiniMaxMusic3TextEncode

ModelPreviewOverrideKJ.description: Adds a dedicated live-preview frame on this node, with overridable max resolution. Default ComfyUI preview caps at 512px; this node sends its own preview straight to a DOM widget on the node so pixel-space models (Chroma Radiance, ZImage, HiDream-O1, …) can be previewed at full sampler resolution.

vae.tooltip: Optional LTX VAE for true-RGB previews. TAEHV-LTX = fast tiny decode (VAE pinned to GPU). Any other LTX VAE = full-quality decode via vae.decode() — MUCH slower per step.

jpeg_quality.tooltip: JPEG quality for the live preview transport.

max_resolution.tooltip: Max preview side in pixels for the live widget. 0 = full sampler resolution (no downscale).

model.tooltip: Model to attach the preview override to.

preview_fps.tooltip: Playback FPS for the animated WebP preview. Ignored when preview_frames=1.

preview_frames.tooltip: Frames to sample from each video step's latent for animated preview. 1 = single frame (current behavior, fastest). >1 = animated WebP playing back at preview_fps. Only applies to video models (5D latents); ignored for image models.

suppress_default_preview.tooltip: Suppress the standard sampler-node preview overlay while sampling, so only this node's frame updates. Progress bar still advances normally.

ModelPreviewOverrideKJ.name: ModelPreviewOverrideKJ

PathchSageAttentionKJ.description: Experimental node for patching attention mode. This doesn't use the model patching system and thus can't be disabled without running the node again with 'disabled' option.

allow_compile.tooltip: Allow the use of torch.compile for the sage attention function, requires latest sageattn 2.2.0 or higher.

sage_attention.tooltip: Patch the attention of the model passing through this node to use sageattn. To revert, run this node again with the disabled option. Requires the sageattention library to be installed.

PathchSageAttentionKJ.name: PathchSageAttentionKJ

VHS_LoadVideoPath.description:
Load Video (Path) 🎥🅥🅗🅢
Loads a video from an arbitrary path
[-]
Inputs:
[-]
meta_batch: (optional) Connect to a Meta Batch manager to divide extremely long sequences into sub batches. See the documentation for Meta Batch Manager
[-]
vae: (optional) If provided the node will output latents instead of images. This drastically reduces the required RAM (not VRAM) when working with long (100+ frames) sequences
Using this is strongly encouraged unless connecting to a node that requires a blue image connection such as Apply Controllnet
[-]
Outputs:
[-]
IMAGE: The loaded images
[-]
frame_count: The length of images just returned
[-]
audio: The audio from the loaded video
[-]
video_info: Exposes additional info about the video such as the source frame rate, or the total length
[-]
LATENT: The loaded images pre-converted to latents. Only available when a vae is connected
[-]
Widgets:
[-]
video: The video file to be loaded.
You can also select an image to load it as a single frame
This is a VHS_PATH input. When edited, it provides a list of possible valid files or directories
The current top-most completion may be selected with Tab
You can navigate up a directory by pressing Ctrl+B (or Ctrl+W if supported by browser)
The filter on suggested file types can be disabled by pressing Ctrl+G.
If converted to an input, this functions as a string
[-]
force_rate: Drops or duplicates frames so that the produced output has the target frame rate. Many motion models are trained on videos of a specific frame rate and will give better results if input matches that frame rate. If set to 0, all frames are returned. May give unusual results with inputs that have a variable frame rate like animated gifs. Reducing this value can also greatly reduce the execution time and memory requirements.
[-]
force_size: Previously was used to provide suggested resolutions. Instead, custom_width and custom_height can be disabled by setting to 0.
[-]
custom_width: Allows for an arbitrary width to be entered, cropping to maintain aspect ratio if both are set
[-]
custom_height: Allows for an arbitrary height to be entered, cropping to maintain aspect ratio if both are set
[-]
frame_load_cap: The maximum number of frames to load. If 0, all frames are loaded.
[-]
skip_first_frames: A number of frames which are discarded before producing output.
[-]
select_every_nth: Similar to frame rate. Keeps only the first of every n frames and discard the rest. Has better compatibility with variable frame rate inputs such as gifs. When combined with force_rate, select_every_nth_applies after force_rate so the resulting output has a frame rate equivalent to force_rate/select_every_nth. select_every_nth does not apply to skip_first_frames
[-]
format: Updates other widgets so that only values supported by the given format can be entered and provides recommended defaults.
[-]
videopreview: Displays a preview for the selected video input. Will only be shown if Advanced Previews is enabled. This preview will reflect the frame_load_cap, force_rate, skip_first_frames, and select_every_nth values chosen. If the video has audio, it will also be previewed when moused over. Additional preview options can be accessed with right click.
VHS_LoadVideoPath.name: VHS_LoadVideoPath

VHS_VideoCombine.description:
Video Combine 🎥🅥🅗🅢
Combine an image sequence into a video
[-]
Inputs:
[-]
images: The images to be turned into a video
[-]
audio: (optional) audio to add to the video
[-]
meta_batch: (optional) Connect to a Meta Batch manager to divide extremely long image sequences into sub batches. See the documentation for Meta Batch Manager
[-]
vae: (optional) If provided, the node will take latents as input instead of images. This drastically reduces the required RAM (not VRAM) when working with long (100+ frames) sequences
Unlike on Load Video, this isn't always a strict upgrade over using a standalone VAE Decode.
If you have multiple Video Combine outputs, then the VAE decode will be performed for each output node increasing execution time
If you make any change to output settings on the Video Combine (such as changing the output format), the VAE decode will be performed again as the decoded result is (by design) not cached
[-]
Widgets:
[-]
frame_rate: The frame rate which will be used for the output video. Consider converting this to an input and connecting this to a Load Video with Video Info(Loaded)->fps. When including audio, failure to properly set this will result in audio desync
[-]
loop_count: The number of additional times the video should repeat. Can cause performance issues when used with long (100+ frames) sequences
[-]
filename_prefix: A prefix to add to the name of the output filename. This can include subfolders or format strings.
[-]
format: The output format to use. Formats starting with, 'image' are saved with PIL, but formats starting with 'video' utilize the video_formats system. 'video' options require ffmpeg and selecting one frequently adds additional options to the node.
[-]
pingpong: Play the video normally, then repeat the video in reverse so that it 'pingpongs' back and forth. This is frequently used to minimize the appearance of skips on very short animations.
[-]
save_output: Specifies if output files should be saved to the output folder, or the temporary output folder
[-]
videopreview: Displays a preview for the processed result. If advanced previews is enabled, the output is always converted to a format viewable from the browser. If the video has audio, it will also be previewed when moused over. Additional preview options can be accessed with right click.
[-]
Common Format Widgets:
[-]
crf: Determines how much to prioritize quality over filesize. Numbers vary between formats, but on each format that includes it, the default value provides visually loss less output
[-]
pix_fmt: The pixel format to use for output. Alternative options will often have higher quality at the cost of increased file size and reduced compatibility with external software.
[-]
yuv420p: The most common and default format
[-]
yuv420p10le: Use 10 bit color depth. This can improve color quality when combined with 16bit input color depth
[-]
yuva420p: Include transparency in the output video
[-]
input_color_depth: VHS supports outputting 16bit images. While this produces higher quality output, the difference usually isn't visible without postprocessing and it significantly increases file size and processing time.
[-]
save_metadata: Determines if metadata for the workflow should be included in the output video file
VHS_VideoCombine.name: VHS_VideoCombine

VHS_VideoInfo.description:
Video Info 🎥🅥🅗🅢
Splits information on a video into a numerous outputs
[-]
Inputs:
[-]
video_info: A connection to a Load Video node
[-]
Outputs:
[-]
source_fps🟨: The frame rate of the video
[-]
source_frame_count🟨: How many total frames the video contains before accounting for frame rate or select_every_nth
[-]
source_duration🟨: The length of images just returned in seconds
[-]
source_width🟨: The width
[-]
source_height🟨: The height
[-]
loaded_fps🟦: The frame rate after accounting for force_rate and select_every_nth. This output is of particular use as it can be connected to the converted frame_rate input of a Video Combine node to ensure audio remains synchronized.
[-]
loaded_frame_count🟦: The number of frames returned by the current execution. Identical to the frame_count returned by the node itself
[-]
loaded_duration🟦: The duration in seconds of returned images after accounting for frame_load_cap
[-]
loaded_width🟦: The width of the video after scaling. These coordinates are in image space even if loading to latent space
[-]
loaded_height🟦: The height of the video after scaling. These coordinates are in image space even if loading to latent space
VHS_VideoInfo.name: VHS_VideoInfo
